content: While taking this medication, it is essential to monitor your liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides, cholesterol, and blood sugar levels through regular laboratory tests. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication and you are taking it twice daily, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. However, if it is less than six hours before your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. If you are taking this medication once daily and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 12 hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, keep it in its original container and do not refrigerate or freeze it. Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. This medication, commonly known by the brand name Prezista, is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. Darunavir belongs to a class of drugs called protease inhibitors. It must be taken with certain other medications, such as cobicistat or ritonavir, to boost its levels in the body. However, darunavir is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. If you are using the liquid form, carefully follow the instructions for use. Take this medication by mouth with food as directed by your doctor. Darunavir must be taken at the same time as certain other medications, usually once or twice daily. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage is based on your age, laboratory test results, medical condition, and response to treatment. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it or other HIV medications without your doctor’s approval. Darunavir may cause side effects such as diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and headache. These side effects are usually mild, but if they persist or worsen, inform your doctor. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. In some cases, your immune system may become overactive, leading to symptoms that require medical attention. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Rarely, this medication may cause an increase in blood sugar levels, which can lead to or worsen diabetes. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly and share the results with your doctor. Darunavir may also rarely cause serious, potentially fatal liver problems. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet known. Darunavir can commonly cause a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. If you develop a rash, contact your doctor immediately. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but require immediate medical attention. Before taking darunavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. If you are pregnant, discuss the risks and benefits of using this medication with your doctor. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Darunavir can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of darunavir from your body, altering its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, garlic supplements, certain rifamycins (rifampin, rifapentine), and St. John’s wort. This medication may also reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In case of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Regular laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides, cholesterol, and blood sugar levels, are necessary while taking this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled.
